• Oxidation is characterized by the loss of electrons by a substance, increasing its oxidation state.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a decomposition reaction that occurs due to the application of electric current?

options.text: Decomposition of sodium bicarbonate by heat
Decomposition of potassium permanganate by heat

questions.solution:

__
 
• Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction where water (H₂O) is broken down into hydrogen gas (H₂) and oxygen gas (O₂) through the application of electric current.
 
• This process involves the use of electrodes submerged in water and a direct current (DC) power source.
 
• At the cathode (negative electrode), reduction occurs, producing hydrogen gas: 2H₂O + 2e− → H₂ + 2OH−.
 
• At the anode (positive electrode), oxidation occurs, producing oxygen gas: 4OH− → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e−.
 
• Electrolysis of water is an important industrial process for producing hydrogen and oxygen gases, which have various applications in fuel cells, welding, and as industrial gases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reaction**

 
 
• A decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• This type of reaction often requires an energy input such as heat, light, or electricity to occur.
 
• Examples include the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂) and the electrolysis of water.
 
 
 
• **Electrolysis**
 
 
• Electrolysis is a process that uses direct electric current (DC) to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction.
 
• It is commonly used in various industrial applications, including the extraction of metals from ores, electroplating, and the production of chemicals.
 
• Michael Faraday formulated the fundamental principles of electrolysis in the 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Electrolysis**
 
 
• Production of chlorine and sodium hydroxide through the electrolysis of brine.
 
• Electroplating to coat objects with a thin layer of metal for corrosion resistance or aesthetic purposes.
 
• Purification of metals, such as refining copper from impure copper anodes.
 
 
 
• **Fuel Cells**
 
 
• Fuel cells use the hydrogen produced by water electrolysis to generate electricity through a chemical reaction with oxygen.
 
• They are considered a clean energy source because their only byproduct is water.
 
• Applications include powering vehicles, backup power systems, and portable power sources.

questions.question: During a chemical reaction, 10 grams of substance A reacts with 15 grams of substance B to produce a new compound. According to the law of conservation of mass, what will be the total mass of the products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 g**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The law of conservation of mass states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in a closed system.
 
• In the given reaction, 10 grams of substance A reacts with 15 grams of substance B.
 
• The total mass of the reactants is 10 g + 15 g = 25 g.
 
• Therefore, according to the law of conservation of mass, the total mass of the products will be 25 grams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass**

 
 
• Formulated by Antoine Lavoisier in 1789.
 
• States that the mass of an isolated system remains constant over time.
 
• Fundamental principle in classical physics and chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Closed System**
 
 
• A physical system that does not exchange any matter with its surroundings.
 
• Energy can be exchanged in the form of heat or work.
 
• Essential for observing the law of conservation of mass.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reaction**
 
 
• A process that leads to the transformation of one set of chemical substances to another.
 
• Involves breaking and forming of chemical bonds.
 
• Examples include combustion, oxidation, and reduction reactions.
 
 
 
• **Reactants and Products**
 
 
• Reactants are the starting substances in a chemical reaction.
 
• Products are the substances formed as a result of the chemical reaction.
 
• The mass of reactants must equal the mass of products in a closed system as per the law of conservation of mass.

questions.question: During the decomposition reaction of lead nitrate, the observed brown colour fumes are of which gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen dioxide gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the thermal decomposition of lead nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂), brown fumes are observed due to the formation of nitrogen dioxide gas (NO₂).
 
• The reaction can be represented as: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ (s) → 2PbO (s) + 4NO₂ (g) + O₂ (g).
 
• Nitrogen dioxide is a reddish-brown gas and is one of the several nitrogen oxides.
 
• This gas is a significant air pollutant and has a sharp, biting odor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lead Nitrate Decomposition**

 
 
• Lead nitrate decomposes upon heating to produce lead oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and oxygen (O₂).
 
• This is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction, where a compound breaks down into simpler substances when heated.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)**
 
 
• Nitrogen dioxide is a toxic gas and a prominent air pollutant.
 
• It is primarily produced from combustion processes, including vehicle emissions and industrial activities.
 
• Prolonged exposure to high levels of NO₂ can cause respiratory problems and other health issues.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition**
 
 
• Thermal decomposition is a chemical reaction in which a compound breaks down into two or more products upon heating.
 
• It is an endothermic process, meaning it requires the absorption of heat.
 
 
 
• **Air Pollution**
 
 
• Air pollution refers to the presence of harmful substances in the atmosphere, including gases like nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and particulate matter.
 
• It can have significant adverse effects on human health, the environment, and the climate.

questions.question: The Chlor-alkali process is used for the formation of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydroxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chlor-alkali process is an industrial method for the electrolysis of sodium chloride (common salt).
 
• This process results in the production of three primary chemicals: sodium hydroxide (NaOH), chlorine gas (Cl₂), and hydrogen gas (H₂).
 
• Sodium hydroxide produced through this process is commonly used in various industries such as paper, textiles, soap, and detergents.
 
• The Chlor-alkali process is one of the most important processes in the chemical industry and is performed using either a mercury cell, a diaphragm cell, or a membrane cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis:**

 
 
• Electrolysis is a technique that uses a direct electric current (DC) to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction.
 
• It is widely used in various applications, including electroplating, electrorefining, and water splitting.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH):**
 
 
• Commonly known as caustic soda or lye, sodium hydroxide is a highly caustic base and alkali.
 
• It is used in the manufacture of paper, textiles, drinking water, soaps, and detergents.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine Gas (Cl₂):**
 
 
• Chlorine is a yellow-green gas at room temperature and is used in the production of a wide range of industrial and consumer products.
 
• It is primarily used in the manufacture of PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and as a disinfectant in water treatment.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H₂):**
 
 
• Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe.
 
• It is used in various applications, including as a fuel source and in the production of ammonia for fertilizers.
